description: Real, first-hand findings on the FTC 'Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees' (effective 12 May 2025) governing US live-event ticket price disclosure, extracted from the us-stats verification pack.
spec_note: REAL-EXTRACT: rows are drawn verbatim/paraphrased from the FTC's own press release (fetched with a browser User-Agent after a 403 on default fetchers) and a search snippet of the companion FAQ page, captured in the 2026-08-23 us-stats audit.

records.finding: FTC 'Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees' — effective date
records.value: Rule takes effect 12 May 2025; FTC press release (dated 5 May 2025) states it 'prohibits bait-and-switch pricing and other tactics used to hide total prices and mislead people about fees in the live-event ticketing and short-term lodging industries.'

ftc.gov returns HTTP 403 to non-browser fetchers; page retrieved HTTP 200 only via curl with a browser User-Agent. The commonly cited slug '/legal-library/browse/rules/rule-unfair-or-deceptive-fees' is a 404 and should not be cited.

records.finding: Rule's legal citation and exclusions (QUOTE-ONLY, via search snippet)
records.value: Companion FAQ page snippet gives CFR cite 16 C.F.R. Part 464 and lists exclusions: government charges, shipping charges, and optional ancillary goods/services. Treat as QUOTE-ONLY until the FAQ page itself is independently fetched.

Any Ticketalay US ticket page must show the all-in total price (ticket + mandatory fees) as the most prominent price from first display; the rule applies to both primary sellers and resale platforms for live-event tickets.
The FTC is a US federal regulator; this rule governs US live-event ticketing and short-term-lodging pricing disclosure only. No UK-jurisdiction rule or FTC authority applies outside the US.
